unreadable-plist-skips-the-bundle: The TS read each bundle's Info.plist with the plist package and let a parse error escape: out of getCrossover's list (the rest of the Spotlight results were dropped and 'CrossOver not found' was logged) and out of getWineOnMac altogether, which rejected the whole of getAlternativeWine so the renderer got no wine list. The Rust discovery skips the one bundle whose plist is missing, unreadable or not an XML dictionary and goes on with the rest. No golden has a malformed bundle plist, so the replay is unaffected; whisky-bad-plist (a readable plist without the version dictionary) lists nothing in both.
steam-libraries-are-an-input: The TS getLinuxWineSet awaited getSteamLibraries, which invoked the Rust steamfiles_read_library_folders channel (the rustInvoke events of the linux-set goldens that name Steam libraries) and filtered the answer through existsSync. The Rust crate reads no Steam file of its own: the shell hands in what that read answered as DiscoveryHost.steam_libraries ({exists, parsed, paths}, or null for a failed read) and the crate applies the same rule (not found or not parsed keeps only /usr/share/steam, parsed keeps the libraries that exist). The replay feeds each golden's recorded answer and makes no invoke, so the rustInvoke events are not compared; the list, spawns and tree are the golden's.
windows-answers-empty: On Windows getAlternativeWine ran the Linux set, creating <tools>/wine and <tools>/proton and scanning PATH for a wine that is never there. The Rust discover_alternatives answers an empty list on Windows and touches nothing. The goldens are recorded on macOS and Linux.
refresh-failure-does-not-reject: When no wine release list was stored the TS awaited updateWineVersionInfos and let a failure (a store file that could not be opened) reject getAlternativeWine. The Rust discover_alternatives logs that failure and discovers what is on disk. A feed that cannot be fetched was already logged and skipped in both. The goldens store a release list, so the refresh branch is 87-07's refresh goldens.
executable-probe-is-the-mode-bits: findExecutableOnPath tested a file with access(X_OK), which asks the kernel about the calling user. The Rust is_executable_file reads the file's mode (any execute bit) because the crate links no libc. The two agree for every file a PATH scan meets (an owner-executable binary, a 0644 file); they differ only for a file that is executable by a group the user is not in.
